dispatch.headline: Support Maggot Refuses Leather Muzzle
dispatch.body: Deep-rock fitter Tomas Cerna has refused three safety orders to muzzle his three-metre flesh-maggot on 16 Psyche. The biological weapon was engineered during the Ceres trade disputes to dissolve heavy metal hull plating. It currently slumps across Cerna's workbench like a giant warm beanbag. "Barnaby is an emotional support animal, and he gets nervous when the drills hum," Cerna explained. Safety officers issued citations after the creature chewed through two hydraulic lifts and a floor beam on Thursday. "That was bad luck because the gravity dropped and he panicked," Cerna said. "A spaniel barks when it gets scared, but Barnaby chews structural steel." Under union rules, support animals are exempt from muzzling if the restraint causes distress or skin irritation. "The leather gives his stomach segments a rash, and he is very sensitive," Cerna said. Cerna bought the creature from a surplus yard last month to manage his severe shift anxiety. "My heart rate is down twelve points since I got him," Cerna reported. "If he eats a spare drill bit, I pay for the bit, which seems fair." Station managers confirmed drilling remains paused while safety officers source a softer muzzle for the larva. They need a restraint broad enough for a three-metre worm that will not ruin its mood. "He sleeps in my bunk because he likes the heat," Cerna added. "My bunkmate now sleeps standing up in the corridor, but he fully supports my mental health."

glossary.gloss: A bio-engineered larval organism designed to secrete acid capable of breaking down metallic alloys.

drafts.headline: Mine Chief Celebrates Filter's Eightieth Birthday
drafts.body:
Shaft Chief Anton Varga marked the eightieth year of Shaft Nine’s bio-filter on Monday by bringing twelve crew members to stand in silence beside its intake valve.

The four-tonne organ processes toxic metal runoff from the lower rock face. Varga insists the pulsing liver-mass is a strict elderly relative named Gran.

"She does not like slackers," Varga said. "Last month we had three line failures on the slush pump. People blamed the seals. Gran knew better."

According to Varga, the filter’s daily bile discharges carry moral guidance.

"If the slime is brown, we are taking long tea breaks," he said. "If it turns yellow, someone lied on a timesheet. She sees everything."

The gathering included a brass band from the ore plant and three hundred kilograms of protein paste shaped like a cake. Crew members watched as Varga fed two slices into the intake valve.

When asked how a brainless organ could hold moral views, Varga dismissed the query.

"My real grandmother lost her wits by eighty," he said. "She still knew if you took extra butter. Gran works the same way."

The filter responded to the cake by spewing sixty litres of burning acid onto the deck. Varga called it a blessing.

"She wants the floor scrubbed," he said. "We start now."
drafts.premise: A drill-rig chief inside the asteroid 4 Vesta has organized an 80th birthday party for the shaft's industrial bio-filter organ, insisting the brainless, pulsing liver-mass is a beloved, stern grandmother whose toxic bile discharges are strict moral advice.

drafts.headline: Mechanic Refuses To Muzzle Support Maggot
drafts.body:
Deep-rock fitter Tomas Cerna has refused three station safety orders to muzzle his three-metre vat-grown flesh-maggot during heavy drilling shifts on 16 Psyche.

The biological weapon, engineered during the Ceres trade disputes to dissolve metal hull plating, currently slumps across Cerna's workbench.

"Barnaby is an emotional support animal," Cerna said. "He gets nervous."

Safety officers issued the citations after the creature chewed through two hydraulic lifts and a floor beam on Thursday.

"That was bad luck," Cerna said. "The gravity dropped and he panicked. A spaniel barks. Barnaby chews."

Under union rules, registered support animals are exempt from air-lock muzzling if the restraint causes distress.

"The leather gives him a rash," Cerna said. "He is very sensitive."

Cerna bought the creature from a surplus yard to manage his shift anxiety.

"My heart rate is down twelve points," he said. "If he eats a drill bit, I pay for the bit. That is fair."

Station managers confirmed drilling remains paused while safety officers source a muzzle broad enough for a three-metre larva that does not ruin its mood.

"He sleeps in my bunk," Cerna said. "He likes the heat."

drafts.headline: Miners Refuse To Scrub Mouldy Duct
drafts.body:
The day shift at Siderite Shaft has laid down their scrapers after air officers ordered the removal of a four-metre fungal bloom from the primary intake vent. Shift supervisor Tomas Osei says the bloom - a cultured spore strain the crew raised - is merely going through a rough growth spurt.

"If you barge in with scrapers while he is forming his skin, he just shuts down," Osei said, pointing to a thick grey mat dissolving a steel strut. "We all remember nineteen. Your sweat tastes wrong."

The bloom covers forty metres of ducting and has turned two air valves into black sludge. Filter teams report heavy spore clouds throughout the living quarters.

"The safety crew keeps threatening him with lye," Osei said. "It is deeply invasive. He is trying to set boundaries."

The strain has already eaten through the outer wall seal of Shaft Four, forcing backup pumps to run continuously.

"He knows the hull is there," Osei said. "He is not stupid. He just wants us to knock first."

Osei said the crew bought the bloom a low-power heater for his growth marker next month.

"He will clear the duct when he is ready," Osei said. "On Monday he pulled back two inches from the fan blades without anyone nagging him."
drafts.premise: Miners in the hollows of Pallas are refusing to scrub a corrosive fungal bloom from the main air ducts, explaining that their sensitive adolescent boy is just going through a phase and will clean his room when he is ready.

quality.judge_reason: It sharply satirises the modern phenomenon of emotional support animal loopholes and workplace compliance logic with brilliantly funny dialogue.
quality.critique: The original dispatch was too short and used overly abrupt sentences. The headline described the setup rather than landing the punchline.
